messages:
celeste: quick sync: postmortem flagged two recurring patterns — inconsistent TTL units during migrations, and gaps in audit logging when keys were mass-rotated. want clear owners + a short playbook so we can close SEC-4821 followups and avoid repeat incidents.

omar: i can take lead on the audit logging gap. i've seen cases where our rotate script bypasses the audit pipeline if run with `--fast` flag. propose we force audit writes via middleware and blockfast in prod until we have test coverage.

jess: i'll own the migration-side hardening for token writes. plan: (1) enforce seconds-only TTL at the writer library boundary; (2) add validation that rejects TTL values outside safe bounds; (3) add an integration test that runs a simulated cross-binary write during migration. target PR this week.

vikram: security ask: for tokens that currently have TTL anomalies, what's the rollback/rotate plan? if >5000 tokens affected we need automated rotate. if smaller, manual targeted rotates ok. we also need a comms plan for services that will see auth churn.

celeste: samplified counts in the ticket show ~2.3k anomalous tokens and a handful of services with high concentration. ops-oncall, can you prepare a runbook snippet for a coordinated rotate with grace window? include steps for pausing pushes, running audit CSV, and re-issuing tokens.

ops-oncall: scheduling a 45m prep call tomorrow 09:30 PT. will draft runbook step:
1) run audit query to export token keys + owning service
2) if count > 1000, trigger automated rotate job with 24h grace; else follow manual rotate subsection
3) enable `AUTH_TTL_STRICT` feature flag in staging and canary for 2h
4) validate audit logs show write events for every rotated token
I'll drop links in ticket.

omar: example audit query i'm testing (redis):
```
# list tokens with suspicious TTLs
redis-cli --scan --pattern "auth:token:*" | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c 'ttl=$(redis-cli ttl {}); if [ "$ttl" -le 10 -o "$ttl" -gt 2592000 ]; then echo {}; fi'
```
This will need batching for scale. I'll post an optimized script in the ticket.

jess: opened runtime PR https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3721  includes TTL normalization, writer-level checks, and an integration harness that simulates migration with two binary variants. feature flag `AUTH_TTL_STRICT` toggles the validation. linking SEC-4920.

celeste: tagging owners + deadlines:
- JESS: merge runtime TTL normalization + integration test (due: 2026-04-04)
- OMAR: audit script + alerting + CSV export automation (due: 2026-03-31)
- OPS-ONCALL: rotate runbook + schedule prep call (prep call: 2026-03-26)
- VIKRAM: comms plan for service owners + risk approval (due: 2026-03-30)

ops-oncall: prep call on calendar. i'll also add a weekly 20m follow-up for 6 weeks to track regressions and make sure runbook remains up to date.

omar: initial audit results posted: ~2300 tokens flagged, distribution skews to 3 services. generating CSV now and will hand off to service owners for targeted rotate.

jess: CI job added: `ci/ttl-unit-test` verifies normalized TTL writes and fails if any test binary writes TTL using ms. left a comment for code owner review.

vikram: approved the controlled rotate plan in the security channel, noted we need to capture audit log IDs for compliance. add a step to store proof artifacts in secure storage.

celeste: will run a 7-day post-deploy check on 2026-04-12 and open a retro note listing any regression signals (auth errors, latency spikes, unexpected rotate fallout). please update SEC-4920 when tasks change status.

security-bot: SEC-4821 follow-ups updated: audit in progress, owners assigned (automated).

jess: final ask  add one-liner to runbook about TTL unit convention ("TTL must be written in seconds") and include the Redis audit snippet. once runbook updated, mark the item done in the ticket. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
